# Tinkrum app patterns

A companion to the Tinkrum app-file guide (tinkrum-app-guide.md). These are structures that personal trackers keep coming back to in the big template galleries (Notion, Airtable, Google Sheets, Microsoft, Apple Numbers), each written as a complete Tinkrum app file that imports with no problems and no design suggestions.

How to use them:

- Pick the pattern closest to what the person wants, or combine two (for example a parent with child logs whose child log has a budget).
- Keep the structure: the tables, the links and rollups, which page lists what and how an entry is added.
- Change everything that is about this example: the app id and name, ids (keep them prefixed by your own app id), field names, choice options, labels, colours and icons, in the person's language.
- The sample apps have no reminders or quick actions; add them as the guide says.

## 1. Log with totals by period

**Use it when** the person records things as they happen (spending, runs, glasses of water, hours) and wants totals for this week or this month.

**How it is built**

- One table with a date (default "today") and an amount.
- A `period` block; the number, chart and list blocks on the page have `source.period: "page"`, so they all follow the chosen range.
- One add button below the list (not a form at the top).

```json
  "version": 1,
  "schemaVersion": 40,
  "app": {

  },
  "tables": [

          "required": true
        },
        {
          "id": "amount",
          "name": "Amount",
          "type": "money",
          "currency": "USD",
          "required": true
        },
        {
          "id": "category",
          "name": "Category",
          "type": "choice",
          "options": [
            {
              "id": "food",
              "label": "Food"
            },
            {
              "id": "transport",
              "label": "Transport"
            },
            {
              "id": "home",
              "label": "Home"
            },
            {
              "id": "fun",
              "label": "Fun"
            },
            {
              "id": "other",
              "label": "Other"
            }
          ],
          "default": "food"
        },
        {
          "id": "date",
          "name": "Date",
          "type": "date",
          "default": "today"
        },
        {
          "id": "note",
          "name": "Note",
          "type": "note"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "pages": [
    {
      "id": "spend-home",
      "title": "Spending",
      "icon": "🧾",
      "blocks": [
        {
          "id": "h",
          "look": "header",
          "show": {
            "title": "Spending"
          }
        },
        {
          "id": "range",
          "look": "period",
          "show": {
            "options": [
              "thisWeek",
              "thisMonth",
              "thisYear"
            ],
            "default": "thisMonth"
          }
        },
        {
          "id": "nums",
          "look": "group",
          "show": {
            "layout": "row"
          },
          "children": [
            {
              "id": "total",
              "look": "number",
              "show": {
                "label": "Spent"
              },
              "source": {
                "table": "spend-entries",
                "aggregate": "sum",
                "field": "amount",
                "period": "page"
              }
            },
            {
              "id": "count",
              "look": "number",
              "show": {
                "label": "Entries"
              },
              "source": {
                "table": "spend-entries",
                "aggregate": "count",
                "period": "page"
              }
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "id": "by-cat",
          "look": "chart",
          "show": {
            "kind": "bar",
            "title": "By category"
          },
          "source": {
            "table": "spend-entries",
            "aggregate": "sum",
            "field": "amount",
            "group": {
              "by": "category"
            },
            "period": "page"
          }
        },
        {
          "id": "start",
          "look": "notice",
          "showIf": {
            "table": "spend-entries",
            "has": "none"
          },
          "show": {
            "title": "Add your first spending",
            "text": "Tap **Add spending** below.",
            "icon": "lightbulb"
          }
        },
        {
          "id": "list",
          "look": "list",
          "source": {
            "table": "spend-entries",
            "sort": {
              "field": "date",
              "direction": "desc"
            },
            "period": "page"
          },
          "show": {
            "title": "what",
            "subtitles": [
              "category",
              "date"
            ],
            "trailing": "amount"
          }
        },
        {
          "id": "add",
          "look": "button",
          "show": {
            "label": "Add spending",
            "variant": "filled",
            "icon": "plus"
          },
          "tools": [
            {
              "do": "create",
              "table": "spend-entries",
              "ask": "all"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "tools": []
}
```

## 2. Category budget against spending

**Use it when** there is a limit per category (a monthly budget per category, hours per project).

**How it is built**

- A categories table with a limit field and a rollup that sums the log for this month (`filter: [{"field": "date", "op": "inPeriod", "value": "thisMonth"}]`).
- The log links to its category with a required link field.
- The categories list shows the rollup as `trailing` with `format: {"kind": "progress", "goal": <the limit field>, "style": "bar"}`.
- A page for one category (`"of"`) with a labelled number and that category's entries, with add-here.

## 3. Goal against progress

**Use it when** the person works towards a target (save $3,000, read 20 books, lose 5 kg).

**How it is built**

- A goals table with a target and a rollup that sums a log linked to the goal.
- Cards with `trailing` = the rollup and a progress bar against the target.
- A page for one goal: a labelled number, then the log with add-here.

## 4. Check-ins and streaks

**Use it when** habits or anything done on some days and counted (drink water, read, stretch).

**How it is built**

- A habits table and a check-ins table: one entry per check-in, linking to the habit, with a date (default "today"). Never one checkbox field per habit: adding a habit would then change the table.
- Rollups on the habit: count of today's check-ins.
- Tiles: a tap creates a check-in for `$row`; `trailing` = today's count with a ring against "times a day".
- A week grid of the check-ins: a row per habit, a column per day; tapping an empty day adds a check-in for that habit and day (`$here`), tapping a ticked day takes it back.
- A week grid on the check-ins (look `grid`): one row per habit, one column per day; tapping an empty cell fills in that day (a missed day too), tapping a ticked cell takes it back with Undo.
- A page for one habit: a streak number and a calendar of its check-ins.

```json
{
  "format": "tinkrum-app",
  "version": 1,
  "schemaVersion": 40,
  "app": {
    "id": "habit",
    "name": "Habits",
    "icon": "🌱",
    "bar": [
      "page:habit-home",
      "ai"
    ],
    "theme": {
      "primaryColor": "#C2562E",
      "mode": "system",
      "colors": {},
      "font": "clay",
      "fontScale": 1,
      "radius": 22,
      "density": "comfortable",
      "cardStyle": "soft",
      "navStyle": "iconLabel"
    }
  },
  "tables": [
    {
      "id": "habit-habits",
      "name": "Habits",
      "icon": "🌱",
      "fields": [
        {
          "id": "name",
          "name": "Habit",
          "type": "text",
          "required": true
        },
        {
          "id": "goal",
          "name": "Times a day",
          "type": "number",
          "decimals": 0,
          "default": 1
        },
        {
          "id": "today",
          "name": "Today",
          "type": "rollup",
          "table": "habit-checkins",
          "via": "habit",
          "aggregate": "count",
          "filter": [
            {
              "field": "date",
              "op": "inPeriod",
              "value": "today"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "id": "streak",
          "name": "Streak",
          "type": "rollup",
          "table": "habit-checkins",
          "via": "habit",
          "aggregate": "streak",
          "days": {
            "date": "date",
            "unit": "day"
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "habit-checkins",
      "name": "Check-ins",
      "icon": "✅",
      "fields": [
        {
          "id": "habit",
          "name": "Habit",
          "type": "link",
          "table": "habit-habits",
          "required": true
        },
        {
          "id": "date",
          "name": "Date",
          "type": "date",
          "default": "today"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "pages": [
    {
      "id": "habit-home",
      "title": "Today",
      "icon": "🌱",
      "blocks": [
        {
          "id": "h",
          "look": "header",
          "show": {
            "title": "Today",
            "subtitle": "Tap a circle to check in"
          }
        },
        {
          "id": "start",
          "look": "notice",
          "showIf": {
            "table": "habit-habits",
            "has": "none"
          },
          "show": {
            "title": "Add your first habit",
            "text": "Set how many times a day it counts.",
            "icon": "lightbulb"
          }
        },
        {
          "id": "orbs",
          "look": "tiles",
          "source": {
            "table": "habit-habits",
            "sort": {
              "field": "name",
              "direction": "asc"
            }
          },
          "show": {
            "title": "name",
            "trailing": "today",
            "format": {
              "kind": "progress",
              "goal": "goal",
              "style": "ring"
            }
          },
          "tools": [
            {
              "as": "tap",
              "label": "Check in",
              "do": "create",
              "table": "habit-checkins",
              "values": {
                "habit": "$row"
              }
            }
          ],
          "opens": "habit-habit"
        },
        {
          "id": "week",
          "look": "grid",
          "source": {
            "table": "habit-checkins",
            "group": {
              "by": "habit",
              "showEmpty": true
            },
            "across": {
              "unit": "day",
              "by": "date",
              "last": 7
            }
          },
          "show": {
            "title": "habit",
            "subtitles": [
              "date"
            ]
          },
          "tools": [
            {
              "as": "tap",
              "do": "create",
              "table": "habit-checkins",
              "values": "$here"
            },
            {
              "as": "tap",
              "do": "remove",
              "table": "habit-checkins"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "id": "add",
          "look": "button",
          "show": {
            "label": "Add a habit",
            "variant": "filled",
            "icon": "plus"
          },
          "tools": [
            {
              "do": "create",
              "table": "habit-habits",
              "ask": "all"
            }
          ]
```

## 5. Recurring due items

**Use it when** something comes back and should not be moved by hand (watering, changing sheets, bills, subscriptions, filters, vaccines).

**How it is built**

- A tasks table with a `schedule` field (`{"repeat": "interval", "every": 7}`, or `monthDays` for a fixed day of the month) whose `lastDone` is a rollup with the latest date of a done log.
- The list sorted by the schedule shows when each is next due and how overdue it is.
- A row button "Done" creates a done entry for `$row`, which moves the next date on.
- A number of what is due this week (`filter: [{"field": <schedule>, "op": "due", "value": "thisWeek"}]`). `due` takes only `today`, `overdue`, `thisWeek` or `pending`; for this month use `{"op": "inPeriod", "value": "thisMonth"}` on the schedule.
- A reminder on the schedule (`when: {"each": {"table", "field": <schedule>}, "at"}`) comes on the due day. For a warning days ahead (bills), use a `date` field "Next due" instead of the schedule: the row button "Paid" sets it a month on, `{"do": "set", "field": "due", "value": {"from": "due", "add": 1, "unit": "months"}}`, with `"also": [{"do": "create", "table": <payments>, "values": {"bill": "$row", "date": "today"}}]`, and the reminder is `when: {"before": {"table", "field": "due"}, "days": 3, "at": "09:00"}`.

## 6. Status pipeline

**Use it when** items move through stages (job applications, orders, leads, projects).

**How it is built**

- One table with a status choice.
- A `board` grouped by the status, with a drag tool that sets the status to `$group`.
- A count of the items that are still open.

## 7. Collection and wishlist

**Use it when** things the person owns, wants or has finished (books, records, wines, places).

**How it is built**

- One table with a status choice that splits want / have / done, and a rating.
- A `choices` block (tabs) on the status, with the list following it (`source.choice: "page"`).
- Counts per status.
- Genres as a choice with `multiple: true` (a book can have several), with a row of genres to tap above the list (`show.browse.filter`).

## 8. Parent with child logs

**Use it when** one thing has several histories (a pet with weights and vet visits, a car with fuel and services, a client with invoices).

**How it is built**

- A parent table and child tables that each link to it with a required link field.
- The parent list `opens` a page with `"of"` = the parent table.
- That page shows each child log in its own section (a header, then the list filtered by `$record`, with add-here) and a chart if the log has numbers.

## 9. Join entries with amounts

**Use it when** two kinds of things pair up many-to-many and each pair has data of its own (a recipe and its ingredients with amounts, an order and its products with quantities, a trip and what to pack).

**How it is built**

- A join table with a required link to each side and the fields of the pair (recipe items: recipe, ingredient, amount).
- The page for one recipe (`"of"`) lists the join entries filtered by `$record`; its add-here is `{"do": "createAll", "pick": true, "from": <the other table>, "values": {<the link to it>: "$row"}}`, so the user checks several ingredients at once (those already in the recipe show as added) and then taps each row for its amount (rule 70). On a calendar the same add-here plans several recipes for the selected day.
- Totals across the pairs chain computed fields: a rollup on the recipe (planned this week) → a lookup of it on the join table → a formula amount × times → a rollup sum on the ingredient, listed with a filter > 0 as this week's shopping list.
